question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}7 \\ 9 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=7 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=9 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=3$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 3(3)-{x}_{2} &=4 \\ -{x}_{2} &=-5 \\ {x}_{2} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5$ into the second equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=9 \\ -2(3)+3(5) &=9 \\ 9 &=9\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=5$, which means

$$
3{a}_{1}+5{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(3)+(5)=8.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -29\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -29\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -29\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-13 \\ 17 \\ -29\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-13 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=17 \\ 3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-29\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} &=-9\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-9$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=17 \\ -2{x}_{1}-3(-9) &=17 \\ -2{x}_{1} &=-10 \\ {x}_{1} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=-9$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-29 \\ 3(5)+5(-9) &=-29 \\ -30 &=-29\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-8 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ -{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=2$.

Substituting ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ 3{x}_{1}-8(2) &=-1 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=15 \\ {x}_{1} &=5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ -2(5)+4(2) &=-2 \\ -2 &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=5$ and ${x}_{2}=2$, which means

$$
5{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(5)+(2)=7.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 5{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=3 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13{x}_{2} &=13 \\ {x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=3 \\ -{x}_{1}+4(1) &=3 \\ -{x}_{1} &=-1 \\ {x}_{1} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=1$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=6 \\ 5(1)+2(1) &=6 \\ 7 &=6\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -12 \\ -15\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -12 \\ -15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -12 \\ -15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -12 \\ -15\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=8 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-12 \\ 4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$, the second equation by $2$, and adding the resulting equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}23{x}_{2} &=0 \\ {x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=0$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-12 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4(0) &=-12 \\ 3{x}_{1} &=-12 \\ {x}_{1} &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-4$ and ${x}_{2}=0$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-15 \\ 4(-4)-3(0) &=-15 \\ -16 &=-15\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.
